purpose: Deterministic E2E fixtures for registration -> approval -> email notification -> requester result.

safety.database: Dedicated disposable test database only; never production.
safety.mailMode: Capture/outbox sink by default; do not send to real employees.
safety.cleanup: Delete only records tagged with this test run ID, using the application's supported cleanup path.

identityResolution.rule: Resolve users/employees/department/positions by business key at runtime. Do not hard-code generated database IDs.

seedUsers.purpose: Submits request and receives final result

preconditions: Verify the listed seed users exist and are active in the isolated database.
Resolve each user's actual department and position; configure the approval policy to match those real values.
Use a dedicated test email sink/address for every recipient; do not rely on production mailboxes.
If a seed user or role is absent, create it through the application's supported seed/test fixture rather than guessing IDs.

requestCases.title: Successful registration, two approvals, notifications, final result

request.subject: E2E approval happy path
request.reason: Automated E2E fixture; no real absence

expected.registration: Persisted once with generated request ID and initial pending status.
expected.routing: Only level 1 is actionable after submission; level 2 becomes actionable only after level 1 approves.

emails.condition: After level 1 approval, if the implementation notifies the next approver

expected.result: Final approved state visible through the requester-facing query/API/UI and approval history records both actors in order.
expected.integrity: One business request; one history entry per accepted action; retrying the same action does not create duplicate transitions or duplicate emails.

expected.registration: Persisted once and routed to level 1.
expected.result: Final rejected state and rejection reason are visible to the requester.
expected.integrity: Level 2 cannot approve after rejection; repeated rejection does not duplicate history or email.

requestCases.title: A peer cannot approve a request outside their authority

expected.result: Forbidden or the application's documented equivalent; never successful.
expected.state: Request remains pending at the same approval level.
expected.audit: Denied attempt is logged if required by the application's audit policy.
expected.emails: No approval-success or final-result email is emitted.

requestCases.title: Email provider failure and safe retry

faultInjection.mailTransport: Fail first send; succeed on retry

expected.businessState: Registration/approval state remains consistent with the documented outbox transaction design; mail failure must not silently corrupt the request.
expected.mailState: Failed delivery is observable and retryable.
expected.retry: Retry delivers the intended notification once; no duplicate final result email.
expected.safety: Fault injection must use a fake/captured mail transport, not production SMTP.

requestCases.title: Double-click/retry registration does not create duplicate requests

expected.businessRecords: One request if an idempotency key/duplicate rule is part of the contract; otherwise assert the explicitly documented duplicate-submission behavior.

evidenceRequiredPerCase: HTTP status and sanitized response body for submit, approve/reject, and requester result query
Persisted request status and approval-history rows before/after each transition
Captured email outbox records: event, recipient, count, correlation/request ID, delivery status
Cleanup outcome limited to the test run's tagged data
